question: Why do games slip into total absorption more easily than most office tasks?
answer: Because a game reports back instantly. Nakamura and Csikszentmihalyi list clear goals and immediate feedback among the conditions of flow: every point in tennis says hit or miss within a second. Most work answers weeks later, if at all, so attention wanders. Shortening the loop is how to borrow sport's focus.
move: Shorten the gap between doing something and learning how it went.
ask: How could I find out sooner whether what I am doing is working?
source: Nakamura & Csikszentmihalyi, Handbook of Positive Psychology, 2002
reference: Jeanne Nakamura & Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, The concept of flow, in Snyder & Lopez (eds), Handbook of Positive Psychology, Oxford University Press, 2002
